q: A `for ... else` runs its `else` clause when
options: The loop finished without hitting a `break`
why: An empty collection completes without breaking, so the `else` runs. Read it as "if we got all the way through without finding anything".

q: How do you break out of two nested loops?
options: Put them in a function and `return`
why: Python has no labelled break. A flag, or flattening with `itertools.product`, are the other two honest options.

q: In a `match`, `case RED:` where `RED` is a module-level constant
why: A bare name in a pattern is a capture. If any case follows it, Python refuses to compile with "makes remaining patterns unreachable".
